hypotheses.binder: (hpos : 0 < Module.finrank (IntermediateField.adjoin kk {(jbar N kk : Fb)}) Fb)
hypotheses.justification: `hpos` follows from `hfin` and the variables already in context. Since `[Algebra ℚ L]`, `L` has characteristic zero (Mathlib's `algebraRat.charZero`), and with `[NeZero N]` this gives `(N : L) ≠ 0` by `Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (NeZero.ne N)`. The imported theorem `ModularCurve.finrank_adjoin_jqModC_modularFunctionFieldFullC_eq_dedekindPsi L N hN` then gives `finrank (adjoin L {jF N}) FF = dedekindPsi N`. Carrying this over to `FF` is exactly what the later lemma `finrank_adjoin_jF` (same file) does, but its proof only uses things that come before this theorem: `laurentBaseChange_eq_fullC` (line 369), `coe_jF` (line 583), and the one-line `subst` lemma `finrank_adjoin_transport`. So it can be inlined. Next, `dedekindPsi N > 0` has a self-contained proof (`dedekindPsi_pos`: the divisor 1 contributes `N / 1 = N > 0` to the sum). Hence `0 < finrank K0 FF`, and rewriting with `hfin` gives `0 < finrank K0' Fb`, which is `hpos`. The rest of the proof is unchanged: replace `hpos` by this derived fact. The degenerate case cannot occur: `N ≠ 0` by `NeZero`, and the characteristic of `L` is forced to be 0.
